Bangladesh, Lithuania seek to leverage strategic positions to boost connectivity, cooperation
item.description:
Bangladesh and Lithuania on Thursday agreed to leverage their strategic geographic positions in the Baltic region and South and Southeast Asia to promote cooperation, stability and inter-regional connectivity.
They also agreed to celebrate the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027 in a befitting manner, highlighting the achievements of the bilateral relationship and reaffirming their commitment to further strengthen ties.
The two sides agreed to encourage greater private-sector interaction and exchanges of business delegations to realize the potential for expanded economic cooperation.
The agreements came at the second Foreign Office Consultations (FOC) between Bangladesh and Lithuania held in Dhaka, where both sides placed high priority to recalibrating and expanding bilateral relations, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Ambassador Dr M Nazrul Islam, Secretary, Bilateral (East & West) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Lithuanian Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs Vidmantas Verbickas led their respective delegations.
Representatives from the Ministry of Commerce, Invest Bangladesh Authority, the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, and the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology also participated in the consultations on behalf of Bangladesh.
At the outset of the consultations, the heads of the two delegations signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the FOC.
The delegations discussed the full range of bilateral relations and stressed the need to further deepen political cooperation. They also proposed reciprocal high-level visits, including by foreign ministers.
Bangladesh highlighted its strengths in key manufacturing sectors, including ready-made garments (RMG), jute and jute products, and pharmaceuticals.
It invited Lithuanian investors to explore the investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh’s Special Economic Zones and urged the early conclusion of an MoU between the apex chambers of commerce of the two countries.
Bangladesh also invited an exploratory mission from the Lithuanian private sector.
Both sides emphasized cooperation in ICT, digital governance, interoperability, e-ID systems, secure data exchange, innovation and business partnerships.
Lithuania expressed its readiness to support e-governance initiatives in Bangladesh.
The delegations also discussed expanding cooperation in information technology, e-registration, e-governance, financial technology (FinTech), GovTech, cloud and data services, cybersecurity, e-transportation, digitization of transport systems, artificial intelligence, innovative technologies, high-tech medical devices, pharmaceuticals and biotechnology.
The Lithuanian vice-minister highlighted Lithuania’s capabilities in these specialized sectors and expressed keen interest in expanding cooperation with Bangladesh, describing it as a rapidly growing digital economy.
The Lithuanian delegation said many Lithuanian digital-sector companies and investors are eager to explore opportunities for investment in Bangladesh and collaborate with Bangladeshi counterparts.
The two sides also discussed cooperation on employment and skilled manpower migration. Bangladesh highlighted its growing pool of skilled workers, including IT professionals, engineers, electricians, plumbers and healthcare workers.
They discussed enhanced cooperation on skilled manpower migration from Bangladesh to Lithuania under the EU’s Talent Partnership program, particularly in ICT, caregiving, construction, hospitality and tourism, agriculture and agro-processing.
Lithuania expressed optimism about the prospects under a government-to-government (G2G) mechanism and through regular legal channels.
The two sides also emphasized the importance of broader people-to-people ties through cooperation in education and sports, exchanges of students, youths, tourists and cultural troupes, and employment opportunities for highly skilled and semi-skilled Bangladeshi workers in Lithuania.
The Lithuanian vice-minister said the number of Bangladeshi students in Lithuania has increased more than fourfold in recent years, with around 1,200 students currently studying at Lithuanian universities.
Bangladesh and Lithuania also agreed to deepen regional and global coordination and reaffirm close coordination and mutual support at international platforms, including the United Nations.
They exchanged views on critical regional and global developments and decided to hold the third round of the Foreign Office Consultations in Vilnius at a mutually convenient time.

item.title: Protest erupts over DP World deal to operate NCT, police disperse protesters
item.description:
A protest erupted in Dhaka on Thursday over the decision to hand over operation of Chittagong Port’s New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) to Dubai-based DP World for 15 years, with police dispersing protesters and allegedly using batons against them.
The protest was organized in front of the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), now operating under the name Invest Bangladesh, in Agargaon, where the concession agreement between the government and DP World was signed later in the afternoon.
Activists of the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) march in Dhaka protesting the proposed lease of Chittagong Port’s New Mooring Terminal to DP World. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Protesters from the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB), Bangladesh Samajtantrik Dal (BASAD) and several other organizations gathered at the venue from around 2pm, opposing the agreement and demanding that the government reconsider the decision.
Police reportedly dispersed the protesters at around 2:45pm.
The CPB said several of its leaders and activists, including party President Sazzad Zahir Chandan, were injured during the baton charge.
Speaking to the media, Sazzad Zahir Chandan said the protest was organized by the Anti-Imperialist and Anti-War Coalition to oppose the agreement with DP World.
“We came here to protest against the agreement with DP World for operating the New Mooring Container Terminal. We believe this agreement amounts to selling off Bangladesh,” he said.
He alleged that the protest was peaceful until police intervened.
“We were holding a peaceful program. At one point, police baton-charged us without any provocation,” he said.
Police disperse protesters with batons during a demonstration against the DP World-NCT deal in Dhaka’s Agargaon on Thursday. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Chandan said the left-wing parties would continue protesting against what they described as the transfer of control over a strategically important national asset to a foreign operator.
“We will remain in the streets. We will fight to protect the country’s ports and national resources, even with our last drop of blood,” he said.
The protesters have raised concerns about the implications of allowing a foreign company to operate a strategically important container terminal at Chittagong Port.
Chandan also alleged that DP World has links with the US Navy and argued that handing over the NCT could create risks for Bangladesh’s sovereignty and national security.
However, such claims regarding DP World’s alleged US Navy links and their implications for Bangladesh have not been independently established in connection with the NCT agreement.
The protesters are demanding greater scrutiny of the agreement, particularly its provisions concerning national security, revenue sharing, investment, operational control and the protection of workers’ rights.
The concession agreement was signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Agargaon at around 3:30pm on Thursday.
Under the agreement, DP World will operate the NCT for 15 years.
The NCT is one of the key container-handling facilities at Chittagong Port, Bangladesh’s principal maritime gateway for international trade.
The decision to bring an international terminal operator into the management of the facility has been presented as part of efforts to improve operational efficiency, introduce international expertise and strengthen port capacity.
But opponents argue that economic efficiency cannot be considered in isolation from questions of strategic control, national security, transparency and Bangladesh’s long-term economic interests.
The agreement has also triggered demands for the government to make its full terms publicly available.
Among the key questions being raised are how much DP World will invest, how revenues will be shared between the operator and the port authority, what fees or concessions the company will receive, and what will happen to the terminal and its assets when the 15-year concession expires.
Questions have also been raised over the selection process, including whether the operator was selected through a competitive and transparent international bidding process and whether an independent assessment of the agreement’s economic impact was conducted.
The status and future rights of workers currently associated with the terminal are another issue likely to come under scrutiny.
Chittagong Port handles the overwhelming majority of Bangladesh’s seaborne trade, making its terminals critical to the country’s economy and supply chains.
The NCT is an important component of the port’s container-handling capacity. Any long-term concession involving its operation therefore carries implications beyond ordinary commercial management.
Supporters of the arrangement are likely to argue that the involvement of an experienced global port operator could improve productivity, technology adoption and service quality.
Critics, however, say the government must demonstrate that the agreement provides adequate safeguards for Bangladesh’s financial, strategic and national interests.
The alleged baton charge has added a political dimension to the controversy. The CPB said the police action was disproportionate and that several protesters were injured.
Questions remain over what prompted the police intervention, whether protesters were given adequate notice to leave the area and whether any specific public-order concerns had arisen before force was used.
A detailed statement from police explaining the circumstances surrounding the dispersal was not immediately available.
With the 15-year concession now signed, the debate is likely to shift from whether DP World should be involved in NCT operations to the specific terms under which it will operate the terminal.
For the government, the central challenge will be demonstrating that the arrangement delivers measurable improvements in port efficiency and trade competitiveness.
For opponents, the focus will remain on transparency, national control, revenue, security and the long-term implications of foreign management of strategic infrastructure.
The publication of the complete concession agreement, including its financial, operational and security provisions, could provide the clearest basis for assessing whether the deal serves Bangladesh’s long-term national interest.

item.title: Navy deployed for 22-day Ilish conservation campaign
item.description:
The Bangladesh Navy has been deployed in sea, river and coastal areas to implement the government’s 22-day “Mother Ilish Conservation Campaign-2026” from October 8 to 29 during the peak breeding season of Ilish.
During the campaign, fishing, transport, storage, buying, selling and exchange of Ilish will be completely prohibited. Fishing of all species, including Ilish, by all fishing vessels has also been prohibited in designated marine fishing areas.
Under “In Aid to Civil Power,” Bangladesh Navy ships and contingents have been deployed for patrol and monitoring operations in 9 districts to implement the campaign.
Bangladesh Navy ships and maritime patrol aircraft are conducting round-the-clock surveillance to prevent illegal entry by domestic and foreign fishing vessels and fishers into the deep sea.
Ships, craft, boats and contingents of the Bangladesh Navy Fleet have been deployed in the sea, coastal areas and the country’s inland rivers, including the main Ilish breeding grounds.
In close coordination with the local administration, armed forces, Coast Guard, Naval Police and fisheries authorities, the Navy will work to prevent illegal Ilish fishing and the entry of foreign fishing trawlers.
During the campaign, strict enforcement will be carried out against individuals involved in illegal Ilish fishing and mechanized fishing vessels. Awareness campaigns will also be conducted.
The Bangladesh Navy has regularly played a role in protecting Ilish breeding grounds, creating favorable conditions for uninterrupted breeding and conserving mother Ilish as a national economic resource.
The Navy is continuing its efforts to ensure the safe breeding of Ilish in the country’s maritime boundary and inland rivers and to protect fisheries resources.

item.title: Minister Anee expects new Ganges water sharing treaty before December 12
item.description:
Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee Thursday expressed hope that a new Ganges water sharing treaty with India would be signed before December 12 this year.
"Restoring the guarantee clause, as in the 1977 agreement, is one of Bangladesh's top priorities in the new treaty," Anee told reporters after a seminar titled "Rethinking the Future of Water: Youth Leadership, Justice and Cooperation," organized by Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS).
The minister said the existing 30-year agreement would expire on December 12. "A five-year agreement signed in 1977 during the tenure of then president Ziaur Rahman contained a guarantee clause but the provision was dropped when the new treaty was signed in 1996."
"We must conclude a new Ganges water treaty before December 12," Anee said, adding that Bangladesh and India are working regularly through the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC).
"Based on meetings between the two countries, Bangladesh is optimistic that the new treaty will be finalized ahead of the deadline,” said the minister.
The minister also said work on the Padma Barrage would become visible between January and March next year.
The government is also moving ahead with a plan to complete the feasibility study of the Teesta multipurpose project and begin main construction in 2027, he added.
Describing the Padma Barrage and the Teesta Master Plan as mega projects of great importance, Anee said about one-third of the country's population would benefit once they are implemented.
The Padma Barrage project has already been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC), he added.
"We hope the work will become visible sometime in January, February or March next year," he said.
On the Teesta Master Plan, the minister said it was another major challenge for the government.
"The Teesta is a swift-flowing river, and people in the downstream areas have long been suffering because of water coming from upstream," he said, stressing the need for technical support from local and foreign experts.
He said discussions have been held with experts of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), who have been given responsibility in this regard, while many other local and international experts have also been consulted.
"The feasibility study of the Teesta project will begin very soon, and main work will start based on that study," he said, expressing hope that the necessary work, including the feasibility study, would be completed in 2027 and the main work launched in the same year.
Asked whether there was any foreign pressure or obstacle regarding the Padma Barrage and Teesta projects, the minister said people living along the Padma and the Teesta are citizens of Bangladesh.
"The interests and expectations of the people of the country are the biggest concern for me," he said, adding that the government's main goal was to work for their welfare.
Speaking about the progress of the Padma Barrage, he said the project's feasibility study took a long time, from 2004 to 2016, and was not implemented afterwards.
"The present government finalized the matter and started work within a few months of taking office," he said.
Noting that a study for a project as large as the Teesta cannot be completed overnight or in a month or two, the minister said previous authorities did not seek adequate technical support to finish the job.
"The present government wants to complete the necessary work on its own initiative and give the Teesta project a visible shape," he added.

item.title: PM chairs meeting on Dhaka's public transport management
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday chaired a meeting to discuss Dhaka’s public transport management, road safety and ways to address disorder in the capital’s transport system.
The meeting began at the Cabinet Division of the Secretariat in the morning, said a release issued by the PM’s press wing.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, State Minister for Road Transport and Bridges Habibur Rashid, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister ABM Abdus Sattar, Local Government Division Secretary Md Shahidul Hasan, Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority Executive Director Mohammad Mashiur Rahman, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque and Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, among others, attended the meeting.
The meeting is discussing various issues relating to the management of public transport in Dhaka, ensuring road safety and resolving the existing disorder in the city’s public transport system.

item.title: Muktadir: Govt working to keep essentials affordable during Ramadan
item.description:
The government is taking various measures to ensure adequate supplies of essential commodities and reasonable prices for consumers during the upcoming Ramadan, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Thursday.
Initiatives are being taken to rationalize duties on fruits and dates, lower interest rates on bank loans for importing consumer goods, and remove obstacles to transportation and clearance of imported products, he said.
The minister made the comments while speaking at a discussion with traders and importers on ensuring the supply of essential commodities and market stability, organised by the Chittagong Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCCI) at the World Trade Center in Chittagong.
The government will also continue regular market monitoring to prevent artificial crisis and unjustified price hikes, he said.
Regarding preparations for Ramadan, Muktadir said there are already sufficient supplies of essential commodities, including edible oil and sugar, while opening letters of credit (LCs) for imports is continuing as normal.
He said the government is working in coordination with relevant agencies to ensure smooth supply of essential goods throughout the year, including during Ramadan.
The minister stressed the need to reduce import costs to keep prices of essentials at a reasonable level.
The government is working to reduce the duty on the import of fruits, currently at 121%, to make them more affordable, he said, adding that a letter has also been sent to the National Board of Revenue (NBR) seeking a reduction in duties on dates.
Muktadir said he will discuss with the Bangladesh Bank governor the possibility of reducing interest rates on bank loans for importing consumer goods.
Responding to a question about unusually high fruit prices, he said selling imported oranges at Tk400-500 per kg even after payment of duties is unacceptable.
The minister, however, claimed that the price has fallen significantly following drives by the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP) and the administration.
“Artificial crisis or attempts to make excessive profits ahead of Ramadan or on any other occasion will not be tolerated,” he said, adding that market monitoring will continue throughout the year.
On reducing supply costs, Muktadir said initiatives have been taken to improve the efficiency of Chittagong Port and remove obstacles to the transport system with a view to bringing down the country's logistics costs from 16%.
He also highlighted several government initiatives to simplify business operations, including making the trade licence system fully online so that certificates can be downloaded from anywhere after payment of the prescribed fee.
The government is also working to modernise the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC) on the model of Singapore and introduce a system for transferring shares remotely through facial recognition and fingerprint-based identity verification, the minister said.
He said the government is also considering making pre-shipment inspection (PSI) mandatory for imports of sodium sulphate, or synthetic salt, and bitumen to ensure quality and transparency.
Asked about the impact of the fuel price hike, Muktadir said the government had subsidised fuel for a long time and made a minimum price adjustment to maintain the country's financial balance.
He said steps are being taken to reduce duties on other imported products to prevent additional pressure on the market.
During the meeting, the business leaders assured the government that traders are fully prepared to maintain adequate supplies of essential commodities during Ramadan.
CCCI President Mohammad Amirul Haque, who chaired the meeting, said traders will ensure that there is no artificial crisis of major essentials, including lentils, chickpeas, wheat, edible oil and sugar.
He said they will regularly monitor market demand and stocks and coordinate with port and customs authorities to ensure smooth clearance of imported goods.
Describing Chittagong as the country's economic hub and an important centre for regional trade and logistics, Amirul called for ensuring a level playing field for businesses in the region.
He also reaffirmed the business community's commitment to conducting trade transparently and protecting consumer interests.
Khatunganj Trade and Industries Association President Abdus Salam urged customs, port and government agencies to strengthen coordination and avoid harassment of traders to ensure smooth supply during Ramadan.
He stressed the need for a cooperative environment for the import and clearance of goods.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,144 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,144.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,040, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Sylhet division with two deaths. At the district level, one casualty each was recorded in Sylhet, Sunamganj, Dhaka, and Khulna.
A total of 1,332 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 201,625.
During the same period, 96 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,116.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 178,927 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 171,680 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Salahuddin: Govt to set up two army camps in hills near Rohingya camps
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the government has decided to set up two new army camps in the hilly areas adjacent to the Rohingya camps to prevent crimes including abductions.
He made the remarks to journalists at the Secretariat around 3pm on Thursday, after a meeting titled “Meeting for the Overall Improvement of Law and Order in Jungle Salimpur, Chittagong.”
The home minister said the two camps would be established in the hills of Rangikhali and Noakhalipara in Teknaf under the leadership of the 10th Infantry Division of Ramu.
He said abductions and other incidents occur regularly in the two hilly areas. To prevent these crimes, a decision has been made to set up two camps in the area under the leadership of the 10th Infantry Division.
The meeting expressed the view that once the two camps are established, such crimes in the area will be eliminated.
He said joint operations are conducted to address the law and order situation inside and outside the Rohingya camps. These operations are being carried out against various crimes, including drugs, weapons and human trafficking.
A deputy inspector general (DIG) of the Armed Police Battalion leads the operations, with other law enforcement agencies also involved.
The home minister also mentioned a decision to rebuild the fencing, or barbed-wire barrier, to strengthen security at the Rohingya camps.
In addition, solar-powered lighting will be arranged outside the camps. Closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras will be installed at fixed intervals, and control towers and watchtowers will be built.
He further said that in the event of a war or any emergency, the army will lead the response. A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been set for this purpose.

item.title: Dhaka, Jakarta discuss visa simplification, boosting trade
item.description:
Indonesian Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Muhammad Anis Matta on Thursday met Prime Minister's adviser and spokesperson for the Prime Minister's Office Mahdi Amin to discuss simplifying visa and travel procedures and enhancing bilateral trade between Bangladesh and Indonesia.
The meeting took place at the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon in the morning.
During the meeting, detailed discussions were held regarding enhancing people-to-people contact, expanding educational linkages and fostering cooperation in the energy sector.
Particular emphasis was placed on the facilities, amenities and safety of the large number of tourists travelling from Bangladesh to Indonesia.
Both sides exchanged views on increasing bilateral trade and creating opportunities for more Indonesian companies to operate in Bangladesh.
Key topics of the meeting included simplifying visa processes, reinstating visa-on-arrival facilities for Bangladeshi citizens and launching direct flights between Bangladesh and Indonesia.
Emphasis was put on leveraging new opportunities for cooperation in potential sectors like trade, investment, energy, tourism, education and people-to-people contact to further deepen the economic and strategic partnership between the two nations.
They also discussed increasing Indonesian investment in Bangladesh and fostering closer ties between the business communities and entrepreneurs of both countries.
Besides, opportunities for expanding trade in ready-made garments, jute, agriculture and palm oil, as well as increasing the export of halal products, were discussed.
Both sides also agreed to strengthen multifaceted cooperation and advance the bonds of shared Muslim brotherhood.
Indonesian Ambassador to Bangladesh Listyowati and Bangladesh Ambassador to Indonesia Md Abul Hasan Mridha were present during the meeting.

item.title: Humaiun: Sincerity needed to resolve water-sharing issues with India
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said sincerity at the political and official levels of Bangladesh and India is essential to finding an amicable resolution to the long-standing water-sharing issues between the two countries.
“If there is sincerity between both countries - at the senior official level, leadership level, and among the water negotiators working from both sides... we have formed a water committee," he told reporters while responding to a question after attending a seminar.
Kobir expressed optimism that the water issues issue could be resolved positively if the leadership of both countries demonstrates the willingness to cooperate.
“If the leadership possesses the mindset to come forward and cooperate, we will certainly achieve an amicable and positive resolution on this issue,” he said.
The state minister said meaningful progress would be possible if there is sincerity between the two countries at all relevant levels, including senior officials, political leadership and water negotiators.
Asked about the broader approach to resolving water-related issues, Kobir said diplomacy and dialogue remain the way forward.
“It is only through discussion, dialogue, and diplomacy that these matters will have to be resolved,” he said.
He also said Bangladesh is taking international law into consideration while dealing with the issues.
“The positions of international law are also being taken into consideration. So, this is where we stand right now,” the state minister said.
Bangladesh and India share 54 transboundary rivers, including the Ganges, Teesta, Brahmaputra, Surma-Kushiyara and Feni, making water management and equitable sharing a key component of bilateral relations.
The Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) serves as the principal bilateral mechanism for discussing shared-river issues.
He said discussions and dialogues on the issues are continuing, with both sides looking into the matters through their respective mechanisms.
“Discussions and dialogues are ongoing and will continue here. From our standpoint, regional cooperation needs to be enhanced,” he told reporters.
The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, signed in 1996. Bangladesh has been seeking a new arrangement that safeguards its interests, including adequate water flows during the dry season.
The seminar was organised to understand water diplomacy on multilateral platforms and identify potential opportunities for Bangladesh to strengthen its efforts and cooperate with other like-minded countries.
The speakers discussed opportunities for inclusive governance and public-private partnerships in transboundary water management; and amplify youth voices in water justice and explore avenues for integrating youth leadership and participation into transboundary water governance and decision-making processes.

item.title: Home minister: Initiative taken to bring Jungle Salimpur under law and order
item.description:
An initiative has been taken to bring Jungle Salimpur in Chittagong under good governance and discipline, with plans to establish a police academy and relocate Chittagong Central Jail there, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said.
He made the remarks to journalists at the Secretariat around 3:00pm on Thursday, after a meeting titled “Meeting for the Overall Improvement of Law and Order in Jungle Salimpur, Chittagong.”
The home minister said a decision had been made to establish a police academy in Jungle Salimpur, modeled on Sarda. In addition, 72 acres of land have been acquired in the area to relocate Chittagong Central Jail.
He said government land, hill-category land and khas (state-owned) land in Jungle Salimpur would be brought under good governance. Space has also been allocated for various forces to ensure the permanent presence of law enforcement agencies there.
Highlighting several decisions of the inter-ministerial meeting, Salahuddin said the meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Chittagong Development Authority (CDA), the Divisional Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner of Chittagong, as well as top officials of law enforcement agencies.
Representatives of the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Armed Police Battalion, Coast Guard and SRB also took part in the meeting.
Salahuddin said the progress of the road network currently being built in Jungle Salimpur was also reviewed at the meeting. Road construction is moving forward in coordination with the Armed Forces Division and under the leadership of the Engineering Construction Battalion (ECB).
The home minister said government land in several mouzas of Jungle Salimpur would be brought under integrated management. A decision has been made to establish a police academy there modeled on Sarda, and the work of identifying land for it is under way.
He said 72 acres of land had been acquired in Jungle Salimpur to relocate Chittagong Central Jail. The jail will be moved to the area beside the Bayezid Link Road.
The home minister also said decisions would be made on the rehabilitation of those who have settled illegally in various parts of Jungle Salimpur. Measures would also be taken regarding the operation of educational and other institutions there.
He said the area would be brought under order by bringing everything under good governance and freeing it from its past as a haven for terror.
The home minister added that, in addition to the police, space had been allocated for the BGB, SRB and Armed Police Battalion to ensure their presence in Jungle Salimpur.
The respective forces will construct facilities on these sites to ensure good governance and law and order in the area.
He said development, government land management, rehabilitation, institutional management and law and order in Jungle Salimpur would be implemented in a coordinated manner.

item.title: CUET standoff persists over demand to reinstate VC
item.description:
The standoff at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) continued on Thursday, with tensions running high as students, teachers, officers and employees demanded the reinstatement of Prof Dr Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem as vice-chancellor.
Students locked the university’s main gate and began a sit-in around 9:00am following reports that newly appointed VC Prof Dr Sheikh Shariful Alam might arrive on campus. They chanted slogans and prevented vehicles from entering the university.
However, Prof Shariful had not entered the campus by 3:30pm and was staying at the Chittagong Circuit House.
Meanwhile, teachers, officers and employees staged a sit-in in front of the VC’s office, also demanding Prof Sayem’s reinstatement.
Academic and administrative activities have remained suspended for 17 days amid the protests. Students alleged that the government had yet to take any initiative to resolve the deadlock.
CUET student Abdullah Al Mamun said Prof Sayem had taken several student-friendly initiatives to modernise the university within 56 days of taking office.
“He was removed without any allegation against him. This is unjust. Our movement will continue until he is reinstated,” he said.
Students began protesting on the night of September 21 against the decision to replace Prof Sayem. The following day, they launched a “complete shutdown”, boycotting classes and examinations and holding sit-ins, human chains and signature campaigns. The CUET Teachers’ Association has also expressed solidarity with the movement.
On September 21, the government issued a notification removing Prof Sayem as VC and appointing Prof Dr Sheikh Shariful Alam of Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) as his replacement.
Prof Sayem was appointed CUET VC on July 27, but was removed just 56 days later, prompting students to launch immediate protests. The ensuing movement has kept the university’s regular academic activities suspended.

item.title: World Egg Day 2026 highlights nutrition, food security
item.description:
World Egg Day 2026 will highlight the nutritional benefits of eggs, their affordability and accessibility, and their role in improving food security and public health, according to a press note by the Bangladesh Poultry Industries Central Council (BPICC) and World's Poultry Science Association (WPSA).
First observed in 1996 following an initiative by the International Egg Commission (IEC) at a conference in Vienna, Austria, the day marks its 30th anniversary this year.
The international theme for 2026 is “Protein That Powers and Protects”, highlighting the role of high-quality protein in eggs in supporting muscle growth, brain development, immune function and healthy ageing. The anniversary mascot, Eggwin, has also been introduced to raise awareness about egg nutrition among people of all ages.
The observance, to be held on Friday, aims to promote eggs as an affordable source of protein and essential nutrients, highlight their importance in meeting the nutritional needs of people of all ages, recognise the contributions of poultry farmers and the industry, and address misconceptions about egg consumption.
Eggs contain high-quality protein and essential nutrients, including choline, iron and vitamin B12, which support muscle development, brain function and overall health.
Choline, found in egg yolks, plays an important role in brain development and nervous system function. Eggs also contain the antioxidants lutein and zeaxanthin, which help protect eye health.
Eggs are widely recognised as an affordable and versatile source of nutrition. Compared with beef and mutton, egg production generally has a lower environmental footprint, making eggs an important protein source in efforts to promote more sustainable food systems.
Poultry farming also contributes to rural livelihoods by providing income and employment for farmers and small-scale producers.
According to the Department of Livestock Services (DLS), Bangladesh produces approximately 24.465 billion eggs annually, averaging more than 60 million a day. Annual per capita egg availability stands at around 137.
The government and relevant agencies are working to increase annual per capita availability to 200 eggs by 2030.
However, rising prices of poultry feed, chicks, medicines and fuel have increased production costs for farmers. Meanwhile, intermediaries and inefficiencies in the supply chain have widened the gap between farm-gate and retail prices, putting pressure on small-scale producers.
Eggs have also been incorporated into the National School Feeding Programme under the Directorate of Primary Education, with two to three eggs a week planned for each student to help address malnutrition and support children's growth and cognitive development.
China is the world's largest egg producer, producing approximately 617 billion eggs annually, according to the information provided in the release.
Mexico leads in per capita egg consumption, with an average of 409 eggs a year. Japan also records high consumption, at around 337 eggs annually.
Annual per capita consumption in many developed countries ranges from 270 to 300 eggs, while availability and consumption in Bangladesh remain comparatively low.
To mark World Egg Day, the Department of Livestock Services, the Bangladesh branch of the World's Poultry Science Association and the Bangladesh Poultry Industries Central Council have jointly taken initiatives to raise awareness about the nutritional value of eggs.
Under the theme “Nutrition in eggs, energy in eggs, and immunity from disease through eggs”, the programs include awareness rallies, seminars and discussions at agricultural universities across the country.
Other activities include distributing free eggs to underprivileged children, orphanages and residents of old-age homes, including in Dhaka, to help improve access to nutritious food.
The initiatives aim to encourage greater awareness of the role of eggs in a balanced diet and highlight the contributions of poultry farmers and the wider industry to food security and nutrition.

item.title: Bus catches fire at Mohakhali terminal
item.description:
A fire broke out in an air-conditioned bus at Mohakhali bus terminal in the capital on Thursday afternoon.
Anwarul Islam Warehouse Inspector at Fire Service & Civil Defence (FSCD) said the fire originated from the bus’s air-conditioning system after it arrived at the terminal from Sherpur around 1:32pm.
Two units from Tejgaon Fire Station rushed to the spot and brought the fire under control at 1:46pm. The fire was completely extinguished at 2:02pm.
The fire might have originated from an electrical malfunction in the bus, the fire service said.
No casualties were reported.

item.title: Driver killed in head-on collision between bus, covered van in Dhamrai
item.description:
A driver was killed in a head-on collision between a bus and a covered van on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Dhamrai, Dhaka, on Thursday morning.
The accident occurred around 7:15am in the Srirampur area of the highway.
The deceased was identified as 26-year-old Abu Bakar Siddique, a resident of Netrokona. A bus passenger was also injured in the accident.
According to Fire Service and highway police sources, a Dhaka-bound staff bus of AKH Eco Apparels collided head-on with an Aricha-bound covered van coming from the opposite direction.
The covered van was badly damaged in the collision, and its driver, Abu Bakar, died at the scene.
Personnel from Golra Highway Police Station and the Fire Service went to the scene after receiving the news and recovered the body.
Traffic on the highway was disrupted for some time following the accident but returned to normal after police removed the wrecked vehicles from the road.
Md Zainul, an assistant sub-inspector of Golra Highway Police Station, said the driver’s body had been recovered.
Police are conducting an operation to identify the bus and detain its driver, he said, adding that legal proceedings were underway.

item.title: Bangladesh, Netherlands discuss trade, migration, regional Issues
item.description:
Bangladesh and the Netherlands on Thursday discussed political and economic developments, the Bangladesh-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), LDC graduation, migration cooperation, human capital development, semiconductor technology, education and sports, and regional and multilateral issues.
The issues were discussed when the Ambassador of the Netherlands to Bangladesh, Joris van Bommel, met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir at the Ministry in the afternoon.
The Dutch envoy briefed the state minister on the upcoming visit of Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation of the Netherlands Sjoerd Sjoerdsma, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The ambassador congratulated the state minister on his recent assumption of office and expressed confidence in further strengthening Bangladesh-Netherlands relations.
He appreciated the Netherlands’ longstanding support for Bangladesh’s development, particularly in democratic transition, trade and investment, sustainable industrial development, water and agriculture.
The state minister also thanked the Netherlands for its continued support to the Rohingya and host communities and reiterated the importance of safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable repatriation of the Rohingya to Myanmar.
The ambassador reaffirmed the Netherlands’ commitment to further deepening bilateral cooperation, particularly in water management, agriculture, shipping, maritime infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges.
Both sides underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement and enhanced cooperation in bilateral and multilateral fora.

item.title: ZCOMMERZ partners with Rajshahi Women Chamber to bring 400 women entrepreneurs online
item.description:
ZCOMMERZ, an e-commerce enablement platform powered by SSLCOMMERZ, has signed a strategic partnership agreement with the Rajshahi Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (RWCCI) to onboard 400 chamber members onto its platform.
The signing ceremony was held in Rajshahi as part of an initiative to expand digital-commerce opportunities for women entrepreneurs beyond the capital.
ZCOMMERZ has also partnered with the Natore Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (NWCCI), onboarding 300 of its members onto the platform.
Bangladesh’s digital-commerce ecosystem has more than 300,000 Facebook-based and online businesses, with an estimated 50% operated or co-owned by women.
ZCOMMERZ enables entrepreneurs to establish and manage online stores without coding or technical knowledge. The platform offers product catalogs, order and fulfillment management, customized store links and secure digital payments through SSLCOMMERZ.
The partnership brings RWCCI’s institutional reach together with SSLCOMMERZ’s technology to provide members with professional digital stores and management tools, allowing them to expand beyond local markets.
Raiyan S. Islam, CEO of SSLCOMMERZ, said: “Being the largest online payment enabler of the country, we have a role to play in building a Bangladesh that is digitally savvy, transactionally liberating, and forward-looking. Our long-proven capabilities and cutting-edge innovation brought the answer in a merchant-friendly solution like ZCOMMERZ. We are delighted to onboard RWCCI as a partner in this journey.”
Rosettee Najneen, president of RWCCI, said: “For our members, this is a turning point. Many of our women entrepreneurs have built their businesses on determination alone, without the digital tools to grow beyond their immediate markets. With ZCOMMERZ, they gain a professional storefront, secure payments, and the confidence to sell nationwide. We are proud to bring this opportunity to the women of Rajshahi.”
The signing was followed by a digital-business capacity-building session covering online store creation, product catalog optimization, order tracking, local delivery management, secure digital payments, online-selling safety, and promotion and customer engagement through Facebook and WhatsApp.
Participants also received a live demonstration of ZCOMMERZ and one-on-one onboarding support.

High school students turn out for new protests across France
item.description:
High school students across France launched a fresh day of protests on Thursday, despite government attempts to ease the crisis which has rocked the country for days.
Students have blocked entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September, and protests have on occasion spiraled into violent clashes with riot police.
Student union leaders urged fresh mobilization across France Thursday, with a rally planned in the capital Paris and national education unions calling a general strike in support.
While many rallies have been peaceful, some demonstrators have started fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police -- with unions, rights groups and the children accusing police of using disproportionate force.
In a televised address Wednesday evening, the prime minister Sebastien Lecornu attempted to calm tensions, promising a plan to respond to the crisis by the end of October.
Although Lecornu denied that security forces have “orders to confront” the young people, many students were unconvinced.
Outside one high school in Rennes, around 60 students had already gathered early Thursday.
Hanaa, an 18-year-old student, told AFP she was “disappointed and unconvinced” by Lecornu’s remarks.
“We expected more from him,” agreed fellow student Salyna, 17, who said they were also disappointed the government response would not be announced until the end of the month.
“This is an urgent situation.”
Suzanne Nijdam, president of university student association Fage, said they did not have “even the crumbs of an agreement” after a meeting with the higher education minister Philippe Baptiste.
She called for protests to continue outside high schools and government administrative offices Thursday, with “larger-scale demonstrations next week.”
As the government tried to adopt a conciliatory tone, education minister Edouard Geffray was to visit a high school in Reims and take part in a “dialogue” with students.
And a fresh meeting between the three main student associations with Geffray and Baptiste was planned for Thursday afternoon.
The students have asked for a direct meeting with Lecornu to present what they say are costed proposals to address their demands.
Student demonstrators -- many attending high schools called lycees for children aged between 15 and 18 years old -- have complained of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures.
Classes were partially or completely suspended in 375 schools across the country on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry.
At a high school in Paris, AFP saw adult protesters forming a human chain with their arms between police and protesting teenagers, who huddled together carrying backpacks and placards.
Access to the school had been blockaded with bins and railings, and AFP saw some scuffles between riot police and protesters.
In the southern city of Toulouse, high school protesters waved the French flag and placards, while graffiti on a school wall read: “The police are cracking down on France’s children.”
Hundreds of students, police and teaching staff have been injured since the protests began, and more than 6,500 people -- mostly minors -- have been arrested.
A 15-year-old lost a hand on Monday after police fired a stun grenade, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told radio broadcaster RTL early Wednesday that he had suspended the police use of stun grenades in response.
Police have opened 18 internal investigations into allegations of misconduct.
The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction.

item.title: Trump to give Musk top US science medal
item.description:
President Donald Trump will present close ally Elon Musk and other tech bosses with the top US scientific award at a ceremony on Thursday, the White House said.
Google co-founder Sergei Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD chief Lisa Su will also receive the National Medal of Science at the “Science: A New Golden Age” summit.
Computer mogul Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will get the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the top award in its field.
“The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation,” White House spokeswoman Liz Huston said in a statement to AFP on Wednesday.
Space X and Tesla tycoon Musk has returned to Trump’s good graces after they fell out last year over his role heading the cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency.
He was also the biggest donor to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.
Musk and Huang were both at Trump’s state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping last month.
Along with other tech bosses they were also at the White House last week for talks in which tech chiefs promised to self-regulate against possible threats from artificial intelligence.
Trump has dismissed warnings that AI could wipe out humanity, insisting it is crucial for what he calls the “Golden Age” of the US economy in his second term.
But Trump’s Republican Party could lose control of Congress in midterm elections next month amid voter concerns over the Iran war and the cost of living.

item.title: Russian strike on buses kills 30 in frontline Ukrainian city
item.description:
Ukraine on Thursday accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians after 30 people were killed when two buses were blown up in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, in one of the deadliest single attacks for weeks.
Photos posted by local authorities showed the burnt-out metal shell of the vehicles, with the blurred-out images of bodies and debris strewn across the road.
Police said the buses were hit with a glide bomb.
The strikes come just a day after five children were among 22 killed when a Russian missile struck a five-story apartment block in Pryluky, in the northern Chernigiv region.
“The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians,” Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin said, accusing Moscow of flouting “every conceivable rule of warfare and norm of international humanitarian law.”
Kramatorsk City Council called it “yet another horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population.”
“Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets,” it added.
There has been mounting concern about the increase in civilian casualties in the conflict, as both sides step up long-range attacks beyond their borders.
Since Russia first invaded in 2022, Ukraine has accused its forces of deliberately attacking and killing civilians.
The United Nations has verified more than 17,000 civilian deaths throughout the war, but says the real number is considerably higher.
Last week, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin had sanctioned massive attacks on civilian areas.
The Kremlin has denied the claim.
Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, has come under increasing attack, including on Wednesday when Russia launched a barrage of powerful ballistic and cruise missiles, and fast-moving, jet-powered drones.
The city’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said two people were found dead on Thursday after a fire at a four-story building that was hit by a drone in the densely populated Solomyansky district.
Klitschko has said the attacks, which have hit key transport bridges in the city, as well as the rail network and energy grid, were “tearing Kyiv apart.”
For the first few years of the war, Kyiv had been relatively spared from the devastation wrought on the frontline but should now be on a war footing, he argued.
Kramatorsk, which was home to some 150,000 people before the war, is one of the key cities that Russia has not yet captured in the eastern Donetsk region, which Moscow claims as its own.
It has been a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military for much of the war and is part of the so-called “fortress belt” which troops are fighting to keep hold of.
Russian forces have edged close to the city’s eastern fringes, which has prompted calls for the civilians who remain to relocate to safer regions of Ukraine.
Filashkin said Thursday’s strike, which happened at 10am (0700 GMT), represented a “sharp deterioration” in security and ordered the suspension of public transport in Kramatorsk and neighboring Sloviansk.
“Under these circumstances, we cannot risk the lives of passengers and drivers,” he said. “The safety of the residents of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk is now our top priority.”
Ukraine last month launched a counter-offensive against Russian troops around Lyman -- to the north of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk -- claiming some success in regaining pockets of territory.

Dhaka ranks 6th globally in air pollution
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 6th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 168 at 9:10am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia ranked first with an AQI score of 225, while Lahore in Pakistan ranked second with a score of 207, followed by Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo in third place with an AQI score of 193.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

Six more children have died from measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,140.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified four of the latest casualties as suspected and two as confirmed measles deaths.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,036, while the number of confirmed deaths rose to 104.
Among the latest fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two suspected and two confirmed deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,280 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 200,293.
During the same period, 110 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,020.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 177,676 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 170,473 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s bail plea rejected in second wife’s death case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam in a case filed over the alleged abetment of the suicide of his second wife, Mariyam Akter.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order after a hearing on Wednesday.
State counsel Harun-or-Rashid confirmed the matter.
Defence lawyers Mahbubur Rahman, Mizanur Rahman and others sought bail for Gazi Nazrul, while the prosecution opposed the petition.
The defence argued that Gazi Nazrul was innocent and had no involvement in the incident. They said he was named in the case to harass him and that police arrested him on September 20 after calling him to the police station for questioning.
They also said police had failed to produce any evidence of abetment of suicide despite questioning him during remand.
The bail petition said the complainant and the accused were relatives and had reached a settlement through family discussions. It said Gazi Nazrul, 75, is a veteran politician and freedom fighter who suffers from a serious heart condition. The defence also argued that he has a permanent address and would not go into hiding or leave the country if granted bail.
The complainant’s lawyers also submitted a settlement agreement to the court.
In the agreement, Mariyam’s father said he had initially filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Islam and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman based on his immediate suspicion following his daughter’s death.
He later concluded, after family discussions and considering other information, that Mariyam had not died by suicide at the instigation of Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda. He said he had no objection to the accused being released on bail.
However, state counsel Harun-or-Rashid told the court that the case was not compoundable despite the settlement.
He said the investigation was ongoing and would determine the facts, including whether Mariyam died by suicide or was killed.
The state counsel also said further information could emerge if Obaidur Rahman was arrested and questioned.
Earlier, on September 30, a court granted bail to Gazi Nazrul’s first wife, Maksuda Islam, in the case.
On September 20, police recovered the hanging body of Mariyam Akter from a flat at NAM Bhaban opposite the Parliament complex. Police later took Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda into custody.
That night, Mariyam’s father, SM Masum Billah, filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Obaidur, accusing them of abetting her suicide.
The following day, a court granted Gazi Nazrul four days’ remand and Maksuda one day’s remand following a petition by Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police Sub-Inspector Md Shamsuzzoha Sarker.
The case was handed over to the Detective Branch that night.
On September 23, a court ordered Obaidur, who had been arrested in the case, to be sent to jail.

item.title: Rajbari’s ilish glory fades as Padma loses depth, current
item.description:
The boats are still there; the nets are still there. But the ilish that once filled the fishing boats on the Padma River in Rajbari has largely disappeared.
Along the riverbank at Bahir Char Daulatdia in Goalanda, rows of fishing boats remain moored. Some fishermen return from the river with their meagre catch, while others sit in their boats repairing torn nets or applying tar to fishing gear under the sun.
For fisherman Shukur Ali Haldar, 75, the scene is a painful reminder of a very different Padma.
“I have been fishing in the Padma for nearly 50 years. We used to get five to seven maunds of ilish in a single haul. Sometimes the nets were so heavy with fish that we could hardly pull them up. We would return to the ghat with boats full of ilish,” he said.
“Now the Padma has neither the depth nor the current it once had. Because of the loss of depth, ilish are no longer found here like before,” he said.
In the past, the river would come alive after dusk with the flickering lights of fishing boats and fishermen would cast their nets throughout the night and return at dawn with boats loaded with fish, he added.
Goalanda’s importance as an ilish landing and trading centre was closely linked to its location at the confluence of the Padma and Jamuna rivers.
During the British period and for years after partition, large quantities of ilish caught in the area were transported by rail to Kolkata.
Local traders said ilish from Goalanda was once shipped in railway wagons to different parts of the region.
But the river has changed over the decades.
Submerged chars have emerged in many places, reducing navigability and altering the river’s flow.
Fishermen said the decline in depth and current, combined with changes in fishing practices and other environmental pressures, has contributed to the disappearance of ilish from the Rajbari stretch of the Padma.
Haldar said he had also witnessed the decline over the years.
“I have caught ilish with fishermen such as Zafar Haldar, Sonai Haldar, Niranjan Haldar and Madan Haldar of Jafarganj in Manikganj. We used to catch two- to three-seer ilish regularly,” he said.
He recalled selling a roughly one-kilogram ilish for Tk 3,600 during the peak season in one year.
But the situation changed after major floods, he said.
“Ilish started declining after the 1988 flood. After the 1998 flood, ilish almost disappeared from the Padma,” he said.
Osel Bepari, former general secretary of the Daulatdia-Debagram Fishermen’s Cooperative Society, said fishermen from Rajbari as well as Manikganj, Sirajganj and Pabna used to come to this stretch of the river.
He said around 40 local boats, 12 boats from Manikganj and 16 from Sirajganj and Pabna were once engaged in fishing in the area. This year, only around 27 local boats are operating, he said.
He said fishermen now have to travel far downstream to find suitable fishing grounds. A boat may get only one opportunity to cast and retrieve its net every 16 to 17 hours.
“With ilish becoming scarce, fishermen are increasingly using different types of nets to catch whatever fish they can find,” he said.
Anwar Bepari, 65, who has spent about four decades fishing in the river, recalled a time when a boat could catch 50 to 60 maunds of ilish a day.“Now you can hardly say there is fish in the Padma.”
He blamed the use of illegal current nets and China-duari nets for destroying fish and their eggs, while also pointing to changes in the river caused by upstream structures and the formation of chars.
“The river no longer has enough water or current,” he said.
Fish traders and wholesalers around Daulatdia Ghat said their once-thriving businesses have also shrunk.
Chandu Mollah, who has been involved in the fish trade at Daulatdia ferry ghat for around 20 years, recalled seeing hundreds of kilograms of fish brought to the market every day when he started working there.
Now, he said, only a fraction of the boats return with ilish.
“At the end of the day, only 10 to 12 ilish may come from 10 to 20 boats. The fish trade has changed completely,” he said.
Badal Biswas, a wholesale ilish trader at Goalanda Bazar, has been in the business for around 35 years, following in the footsteps of his late father, Sadeq Ali Biswas.
“Business was very lively during my father’s time. ilish from Goalanda used to be sent to different parts of the country. It was even transported to Kolkata in railway wagons,” he said.
“Now there is no Padma ilish. Those days are a golden past,” Biswas said.
He has kept the family business going by bringing ilish from Barishal and Chattogram.
Mohan Mondal, president of the Daulatdia Ghat Bazar Business Association, said the decline has been dramatic even in recent years.
“Even six or seven years ago, fishermen used to bring 20 to 30 maunds of ilish to my wholesale shop every day,” he said.
There are now 11 wholesale shops at the ghat, he said, but on a recent day only two shops received ilish, totalling just 2-3 kilograms.
During the peak season, the entire ghat may receive only 10-12 kilograms in a day, Mondal said.
The decline in Rajbari is part of a broader concern over ilish production in Bangladesh.
According to the Department of Fisheries, national ilish production fell to 512,000 metric tonnes in fiscal year 2024-25 from 529,000 tonnes in 2023-24 and 571,000 tonnes in 2022-23.
Fisheries officials and researchers have also pointed to changes in river conditions and the degradation of breeding grounds as threats to the national fish.
Rajbari District Fisheries Officer Md Mahbub Ul Haque said the decline is not unique to Rajbari. Ilish production has declined across the country. Climate change is causing changes in the size and availability of ilish.”
He said the formation of numerous submerged chars has reduced river depth and navigability, while environmental changes are disrupting the fish’s normal movement.
“Human-induced pollution is also a factor. At the same time, catching mother ilish and jatka is having an impact,” he said.

item.title: Seven years on, Abrar Fahad's family still waits for execution of verdict
item.description:
Seven years after the killing of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) student Abrar Fahad, his elderly parents are still waiting to see the execution of the verdict in the case.
A Dhaka court in December 2021 sentenced 20 people to death and five others to life imprisonment in the sensational murder case that sparked huge outcry across the coutnry.
The High Court upheld the sentences on March 16, 2025.
However, the judicial process has not yet reached its final stage as appeals against the High Court verdict remain pending before the Appellate Division.
Abrar’s family said that although verdicts have been delivered at two levels of the judiciary, their wait for the case to reach its conclusion continues.
Abrar’s younger brother Abrar Faiyaz said the killing had a profound impact not only on their family but also on the country’s political and social landscape.
“Fascism’s exit began with Abrar Fahad’s murder. But the trial of those responsible for the killing that contributed to the change in Bangladesh’s political scenario is still unfinished,” he told over the phone.
He said his family contacted the relevant authorities after the High Court verdict in March 2025, but were told that cases are being dealt with according to their serial numbers.
“Cases can be taken up earlier in the serial. But they are hesitant to bring this case forward. We have contacted everyone we needed to. Now there is nothing left for us to do but wait,” he said.
“We do not know what is preventing the execution of the verdict. At this point, it feels like nothing but neglect,” Faiyaz said.
Abrar’s father, Md Barkat Ullah, also expressed frustration over the delay.
“Execution of the verdict against Abrar’s killers is not only my family’s demand; it is the demand of people across Bangladesh. Yet the sentences are not being carried out. I am not the only one disappointed by this — everyone in the country is,” he said over the phone.
“We still have not received complete justice. I appeal to the government to complete the judicial process as soon as possible,” he said.
Barkat Ullah said the family never imagined that their son, a student of one of the country’s premier educational institutions, would be brutally killed in such a manner.
National Citizens Party (NCP) Kushtia district member secretary Sultan Mahmud Talha said the authorities should take steps to execute the court verdict.
“The movement against fascism began with Abrar Fahad’s killing. That system has since been removed, and successive governments are benefiting from the circumstances created by his killing. They should ensure the execution of the sentences,” he said.
Abrar, a student of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department at BUET, was beaten to death at Sher-e-Bangla Hall on the night of Oct 6, 2019.
His father filed a murder case with Chawkbazar Police Station. After investigation, police submitted a charge sheet against 25 BUET students on Nov 13, 2019.
After more than two years of trial, a Dhaka court sentenced 20 accused to death and five to life imprisonment on Dec 8, 2021. The High Court later upheld the sentences after hearing the death references and appeals filed by the convicts.
The killing sparked widespread protests and public outrage and prompted renewed debate over student politics, political influence on campuses and violence in residential halls.

item.title: Three siblings sentenced to death, 10 others get life for killing Mymensingh farmer

item.title: Bangladesh eyes stronger tourism, fisheries cooperation with Maldives
item.description:
Underscoring the potential to expand cooperation with the Maldives in tourism and fisheries, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat urged closer collaboration to promote sustainable fisheries, develop tourism and create new avenues for bilateral engagement.
The minister made the call while speaking at a chief guest at “The Great Tuna Gala – Flavours from the Sunny Side”, organised by the Maldives High Commission to showcase the country’s sustainable tuna fishery, culinary heritage and tourism opportunities while strengthening trade, business and people-to-people ties between Bangladesh and the Maldives.
High Commissioner of Maldives to Bangladesh Shiuneen Rasheed highlighted the close connection between the Maldives and the ocean and the central place fisheries holds in the country’s economy, communities and culture.
She spoke about the Maldives’ pole-and-line tuna fishery and the importance of maintaining sustainable fishing practices, and highlighted the potential to expand Maldivian tuna and other fisheries products in the Bangladesh market.
Distinguished guests at ’The Great Tuna Gala– Flavours from the Sunny Side’ at Sheraton Dhaka, on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. Photo: Courtesy
The high commissioner also noted the growing connectivity between the two countries and the opportunities this creates for greater tourism, trade and business engagement.
The event highlighted the Maldives’ deep connection with the ocean and the important role fisheries continues to play in the country’s economy, culture and island communities.
Tuna, the mainstay of the Maldivian fisheries sector, featured prominently throughout the event, with guests introduced to a range of Maldivian fisheries products.
A particular focus was placed on the Maldives’ traditional pole-and-line fishing method, through which tuna are caught individually.
Practised in the Maldives for generations, pole-and-line fishing reflects the country’s longstanding commitment to responsible and sustainable use of its marine resources.
Renowned Maldivian Chef Maha Naseer, who travelled to Dhaka especially for the occasion, presented a live culinary demonstration featuring Maldivian dishes and showcased the versatility of tuna and other fisheries products in Maldivian cuisine.
Around 250 guests, including senior representatives of the Government of Bangladesh, members of the diplomatic corps, business leaders, tourism and fisheries industry partners, and representatives of the media, attended the event.
Guests were given an opportunity to experience authentic Maldivian flavours and learn more about the close relationship between the country’s fisheries, culinary traditions, island communities and way of life.
The Gala also showcased the Maldives as a leading global tourism destination, highlighting the country’s distinctive island experiences, natural beauty, hospitality and rich cultural heritage.
Through The Great Tuna Gala, the High Commission sought to create greater awareness of Maldivian fisheries products in Bangladesh, explore opportunities for expanding market access and business-to-business partnerships, and further promote the Maldives as a preferred destination for Bangladeshi travellers.
The event reflected the growing economic and people-to-people ties between the Maldives and Bangladesh and the potential for further cooperation in fisheries, trade, tourism and other areas of mutual interest.
The event was supported by Epitychia Holdings Pvt Ltd, VARU by Atmosphere, Maldives Industrial Fisheries Company Limited, Maldivian Airlines, Sheraton Dhaka, THE WAY DHAKA and INZAA Company Pvt Ltd.

item.title: Muhit: Dengue infection rate lower than previous years
item.description:
The dengue situation is less severe than had been feared, State Minister of Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit has said.
The state minister has attributed the lower infection rate to coordinated efforts involving multiple stakeholders.
“The dengue infection rate is lower this year compared to previous years because we have taken initiatives involving everyone,” he said while visiting a vaccination session of the Special Measles-Rubella Catch-up Campaign 2026 at the Korail T&T playground in Dhaka on Wednesday.
The state minister said 20 million children across the country have already been vaccinated under the measles-rubella immunisation program. The government is working to vaccinate another 3.5 million children under the campaign over the next month.
He said the government was working to address challenges in rebuilding the country’s healthcare system.
“Under the leadership of the prime minister, healthcare for the people has been given special importance in the election campaign and manifesto. Alongside disease prevention, the health sector is also being prioritized to increase people’s productivity,” he said.
The government is prioritising the continuation of various vaccination programmes, Muhit said, adding that the US government, Gavi, Unicef, Dhaka North City Corporation and health and field-level workers across the country are supporting the efforts.
Highlighting measures taken to prevent measles, the state minister said work on the issue began after the government took office.
“Through the joint efforts of the health ministry, local government, city corporations and field-level health workers, we have already been able to vaccinate 20 million children,” he said.
He said the government had not stopped the programme after vaccinating 20 million children because “every child’s life is important.”
“The government’s goal is to ensure that not a single child is left unvaccinated. That is why this year’s programme has been taken up as a mop-up campaign,” he said.
Under the campaign, children in remote and hard-to-reach areas, children with disabilities and those who missed vaccination during earlier phases for any reason are being identified and vaccinated.
The state minister said efforts were being made to reach every child.

item.title: Youth shot in Khulna
item.description:
A young man was shot and injured by unidentified assailants in Khulna on Wednesday morning.
The incident took place around 6:30am near the second gate of BL College under Daulatpur police station.
Police and locals said the injured man, identified as Mahidul Islam, works cleaning vehicles at an oil depot behind BL College.
He had gone to a hotel near the college’s second gate for breakfast around 6:30am when around 10 youths surrounded him and opened fire. A bullet struck him in the abdomen.
Locals took Mahidul to Khulna Medical College Hospital for treatment.
Daulatpur police station Sub-Inspector Md Abdur Razzak said police visited the scene after being informed of the incident.
“We are speaking to the injured man at the hospital to understand what happened. We are also trying to collect CCTV footage from the area,” he said.
Mahidul is the son of Shawkat Khan of Bangaon village in Muksudpur upazila of Gopalganj.
The shooting comes less than two days after Aktar Dhali was shot dead in Rupsa, further fuelling concerns over law and order in Khulna.
According to Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP), 38 people have been killed in the city so far this year, with 23 murder cases filed.
Police said they have solved 19 of those cases and arrested 81 people.
A total of 17 cases are under investigation, and two are pending trial.
Police attributed nine killings to family or personal disputes, seven to drugs disputes, two to easy-bike theft, two to unknown causes and one to mob beating over suspicion of theft.
In 2025, at least 39 people were killed in the city and 37 murder cases were filed. Police said they solved 36 cases and arrested 144 people.
Drug dealing and turf disputes accounted for 18 of the killings, while 14 resulted from family or personal conflicts, three from attempts to steal easy-bikes and two from unknown causes.
According to Khulna District Police, 33 murder cases were filed across the district between January and September this year. Seven of the killings involved firearms.
Of the 33 cases filed across the district’s nine police stations, 11 were linked to family disputes, three to drugs, three to robbery or theft, two to turf disputes and two to financial disputes. One case involved an attack on government employees.
Police said they have solved 25 of the 33 cases.
