Dhaka Tribune journalist Shahrukh selected for COP31 fellowship
item.description:
Dhaka Tribune journalist Shaikh Shahrukh Farhan has been selected for the 2026 Climate Change Media Partnership (CCMP) Reporting Fellowship to cover the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20.
Shahrukh is among 14 journalists and two independent creator-journalists selected from Asia, Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Pacific through an international selection process.
The fellowship is jointly organized by the Earth Journalism Network (EJN), Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.
Under the program, the selected journalists will report directly from the UN climate negotiations, covering international climate policy and its implications for audiences in their respective countries.
For Bangladesh, Shahrukh’s reporting is expected to focus on the implications of COP31 negotiations for a country facing climate-related challenges, including rising temperatures, extreme weather, sea-level rise and coastal erosion.
The fellowship will enable participants to cover negotiations and developments involving climate finance, infrastructure, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, mitigation and adaptation.
Participants will also receive professional guidance from journalists and media trainers Joydeep Gupta, Fermín Koop and Imelda Abaño.
The program brings together journalists from 15 countries, providing opportunities to exchange reporting experiences and strengthen their understanding of international climate negotiations.
Other selected fellows include Anandabhuwana from Indonesia, Angelica Maria Daza Romero from Colombia, Aparna Bose from India, Aria Deemie from Liberia, Hammad S from Pakistan, Lerato Mutsila from South Africa, María de los Ángeles Graterol Camacho from Venezuela, Maria Vasileva Petrova-Galabova from Bulgaria, Nadia Luna from Argentina, Nathalie Iriarte Villavicencio from Bolivia, Nkoli Omhoudu from Nigeria, Noel Charles Piringi from Solomon Islands, Francis Ontomwa from Kenya and Zenebe Hailu Gemechu from Ethiopia.
Shahrukh has more than 12 years of experience in journalism, covering public policy, governance, climate change, environmental protection, energy, ICT and telecommunications, elections, migration, women and children, and sustainable development.
His reporting interests include climate adaptation, renewable energy, energy security, environmental pollution, biodiversity conservation, climate finance and issues affecting climate-vulnerable communities.
COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, is scheduled to take place in Antalya from November 9 to 20.
The conference will bring together government representatives, international organizations, researchers, civil society groups and other stakeholders for negotiations on global climate action.
Key issues expected to feature in reporting from the conference include countries’ climate commitments, progress on previous agreements, climate finance, mitigation and adaptation.

item.title: Dinajpur entrepreneur cultivates black rice for first time in Bochaganj
item.description:
A young entrepreneur has experimentally cultivated Vietnamese black rice for the first time in Bochaganj upazila of Dinajpur, drawing interest from local farmers over its potential profitability.
Rakibul Haque, a resident of Dighori village in Nafanagar Union who cultivated the crop on 33 decimals of leased land, said he became interested in black rice after learning about it online. He first bought 1kg of rice for Tk550 to taste it before deciding to cultivate the crop. He later purchased 2kg of seeds online for Tk1,150 and raised seedlings.
Unable to secure permission to use his family’s ancestral land, he leased 33 decimals for Tk24,000 and transplanted the seedlings on July 9. The crop is expected to be harvested between October 10 and 12. “Black rice does not require additional fertiliser, irrigation or special care compared with conventional rice,” Rakibul said.
He expects to harvest 18-20 maunds of rice from the plot. With black rice currently selling for around Tk400 per kg, he expects potential sales of about Tk320,000 if the projected yield and market price are achieved.
According to the agriculture department, black rice is rich in antioxidants, anthocyanin, fibre and iron. Its nutritional value has made it popular among health-conscious consumers, while it is also sought after by Chinese restaurants.
Local residents have been visiting the field ahead of the harvest, and some have contacted Rakibul to collect seeds for future cultivation. Local farmers Shambhu Roy and Jewel said they were interested in growing black rice after seeing the crop’s growth and condition.
Rakibul’s father, Aminul Haque, initially opposed the project, calling his son’s internet-inspired venture “madness” and refusing to provide ancestral land. He has since changed his mind after seeing the crop’s progress. “I am ready to support my son in any way I can after seeing the success of his initiative,” he said.
Bochaganj Upazila Agriculture Officer Nayan Kumar Saha said wider cultivation of the nutrient-rich rice could contribute to the country’s agricultural economy.
Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Maruf Hasan said this was the first black rice cultivation in Bochaganj. “If production and marketing can be properly ensured, it could be a profitable crop for farmers,” he said.

item.title: Fruit prices soar in Bandarban
item.description:
Prices of various fruits have surged in Bandarban, with traders attributing the rise in prices of oranges, maltas and pomegranates to increased demand amid a dengue outbreak.
Prices of oranges and maltas have increased by up to Tk200 per kilogram in the past two weeks, putting fruits beyond the reach of many patients and middle-income families.
A visit to Bandarban’s fruit market on Friday found that the price of malta had risen from Tk270 to Tk450 per kg, while Chinese oranges increased from Tk280 to Tk500. Pomegranates rose from Tk380 to Tk460 per kg.
Gala apples increased from Tk340 to Tk360, Fuji Gala apples from Tk320 to Tk330, pears from Tk300 to Tk310 and red grapes from Tk400 to Tk440 per kg.
White grapes, which were previously unavailable in the market, are now selling for Tk500 per kg. Watermelon prices have also risen from Tk80 to Tk90 per kg.
Mohammad Abdul Alim of Siddiq Store, a fruit trader at Bandarban market, said demand had not increased significantly. “Fruit prices are high because our purchase costs have increased. So, we have to sell them at higher prices,” he said.
Papayas, commonly included in the diets of dengue patients, are also in short supply. Meanwhile, large coconuts have risen from Tk120 to Tk160 each, while small ones now sell for Tk120, up from Tk110.
Champak Das, a coconut trader, said demand for coconuts had increased amid the dengue outbreak while supplies had fallen. “When supply falls against higher demand, prices go up. We have little scope to sell them at lower prices,” he said.
According to the Bandarban civil surgeon’s office, 1,095 people have contracted dengue in the district between January 1 and October 2. Two people have died, both from Rowangchhari upazila.
Akim Bom, who was buying fruit for a patient, said the price hikes were making it increasingly difficult for families to afford fruit. “If prices keep rising like this, we may not be able to continue buying fruit,” he said.
Traders expect prices of imported fruits to ease somewhat toward the end of October as the winter season begins and supplies increase.

item.title: ‘Shanti Nibas’ remains closed for three years in Rajshahi, Khulna
item.description:
A ‘Shanti Nibas’ (old home), built by the government for abandoned and destitute elderly people in Rajshahi at a cost of nearly Tk 9 crore, has remained closed for three years. The Shanti Nibas in Baya area of Paba upazila was inaugurated three years ago with facilities to accommodate 25 elderly people, including healthcare, lift, recreation, exercise, prayer, and training facilities.
But not a single elderly person has been admitted to the facility due to a lack of manpower recruitment. Besides, an organogram for its operation has yet to be prepared.
The facility was built under a government program to provide safe accommodation and care for people aged over 60 who are abandoned, destitute, or have no one to look after them. In 2020, Department of Social Services took up a project to build 25-bed Shanti Nibas facilities on the premises of government children’s homes in eight divisions.
In Rajshahi, a three-storey building with a five-storey foundation was constructed on 1,621 square metres of land on the western side of Paba Government Children’s Home (Boys). It has 25 beds, a lift, reception and visitors’ rooms, a healthcare corner, recreation and exercise equipment, a prayer room, a training corner, a production unit, and a coffee corner.
Despite the infrastructure being ready, the facility has remained closed to its intended beneficiaries. Long periods of disuse have left dust on furniture and equipment, while moss has formed on parts of the walls. Some equipment is also at risk of deterioration.
Rajshahi Social Services Department Deputy Director Monira Khatun said the facility could not be opened because the necessary manpower had not been appointed. “An organogram for recruiting the required manpower has not even been prepared. So far, we have not been able to admit any elderly person,” she said.
Besides, a Shanti Nibas built in Khulna to provide shelter for abandoned and destitute elderly people has remained closed for nearly three years due to a lack of staff appointments and an official office code.
The facility, built inside the government children’s family premises in Maheshwarpasha, was formally inaugurated on November 14, 2023. However, it has yet to accommodate a single resident. The three-storey building, constructed on a five-storey foundation, can house 25 elderly people.
A recent visit found moss on the stairs, balconies and walls, while railings have started rusting. Furniture and equipment have also been gathering dust. Some fire extinguishers at the facility have expired.
The ground floor has a doctors’ room equipped with a bed, wheelchairs and a therapy bed, while exercise equipment remains unused in the gym. The dining room has two large tables.
“The furniture and other equipment are deteriorating to some extent as the facility has remained unused for so long,” said Khan Motahar Hossain, deputy director of the divisional social services office. “It could not be opened due to the absence of staff appointments and an office code,” he added.

item.title: WHO: Heart disease remains world’s biggest killer
item.description:
Ischaemic heart disease is still the world's deadliest condition; meanwhile, Covid-19 has been among the global top 10 causes of death for the first time since the pandemic began, according to the latest World Health Organization (WHO) data released on Friday.
In 2023, the top 10 causes of death made up 33 million out of 61 million deaths worldwide, which is 54% of the total.
Eight of these ten were noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), and they alone caused 47% of all deaths.
Ischaemic heart disease led to 9.5 million deaths in 2023, which is about 16% of deaths worldwide.
Since 2000, deaths from this disease have increased by 3 million, the biggest rise among all causes.
Stroke was the second leading cause, with about 6.8 million deaths (11%), followed by chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at 3.6 million (6%).
Lower respiratory infections were fourth and became the world's deadliest communicable disease again, killing 2.7 million people, which is back to pre-pandemic 2019 levels.
Alzheimer's disease and other dementias were the fifth leading cause, with 2.1 million deaths. Two-thirds of those who died were women.
Diabetes was sixth, causing 2 million deaths, which is more than twice the number in 2000.
Lung cancers were seventh, with deaths rising from 1.1 million in 2000 to 1.8 million.
Kidney diseases moved from seventeenth to ninth place, with deaths increasing by 86% since 2000.
Covid-19 was the top cause of death worldwide in 2021, with about 9.4 million deaths. By 2023, direct deaths dropped to 0.9 million, making it the fourteenth leading cause.
HIV/AIDS deaths have dropped by 62% since 2000, moving from seventh to twenty-second place.
Bangladesh is in the World Bank's lower-middle-income group, where the WHO reports a mixed disease burden.
In this group, five of the top ten causes of death were NCDs, four were communicable, maternal, neonatal, or nutritional conditions, and one was road injury.
Between 2000 and 2023, deaths from ischaemic heart disease, stroke, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease roughly doubled. These now rank in the top three.
Diabetes moved from fifteenth to fifth place, with deaths more than tripling.
Tuberculosis and diarrhoeal diseases are still in the top 10 for this group, but deaths from both have dropped by more than half over the period.
However, the WHO report does not provide country-level figures for Bangladesh.
The report shows big differences by income level.
In low-income countries, seven of the top ten causes of death were communicable diseases, with lower respiratory infections leading for most years since about 2010.
Annual deaths from the disease have exceeded 350,000 throughout 2000-2023, with no notable downward trend.
In upper-middle-income countries, lung cancer deaths more than doubled, with 520,000 more deaths.
Covid-19 is still in the top 10 only in this group.
In high-income countries, NCDs made up nine of the ten leading causes of death.
Deaths from heart disease and stroke fell by 18% and 26%, respectively, since 2000, though dementia deaths nearly quadrupled and it became the third leading cause of death.
The WHO emphasized that reliable mortality data is crucial for setting health priorities, allocating resources, and making policies in areas like transport, food, agriculture, and environmental protection.
However, it noted that data collection remains a major challenge, especially in many low-income countries where systems are often fragmented, incomplete, or inconsistent.

item.title: UK maritime agency: Oil tankers attacked in Hormuz strait
item.description:
Two oil tankers have been struck by "unidentified projectiles" in the Strait of Hormuz region, a British maritime agency said Friday, in the latest threat to shipping in the waterway.
The Hormuz passage, through which a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passed before the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February and sparked the Middle East war, remains at the heart of the conflict.
Tehran has been blocking the passage of commercial ships, firing on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings.
Washington responded with a counterblockade of Iranian ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting its oil.
The first attack caused "a small fire and blackout onboard", the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said Friday, adding that the fire was later extinguished.
There were no reported casualties or environmental impact, it added.
The vessel, which was exiting the strait, was able to resume its journey, UKMTO said, without specifying the ship's ports of origin and destination.
Hours later, another crude oil tanker reported being struck by an "unknown projectile" east of Oman, with all crew safe and no environmental damage reported, according to the UKMTO.
The agency said authorities were investigating the incidents.

Uranium consignment reaches Rooppur nuclear power plant amid tight security
item.description:
A uranium consignment for the second unit of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant reached the project site in Pabna on Saturday afternoon amid tight security.
Three uranium-laden lorries arrived at the nuclear power plant site around 12:25pm after leaving Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at around 7:15am under the security escort of the Bangladesh Army, said Pabna Deputy Commissioner Aminul Islam.
The consignment is the first shipment of uranium for the second unit of the Rooppur plant.
A special cargo aircraft carrying the uranium landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 11:44pm on Friday.
After completing the necessary formalities, the uranium was transported to Rooppur in three lorries while another vehicle carried other equipment.
A team of specialists who had arrived from Russia also accompanied the consignment.
Members of the Bangladesh Army, police and various intelligence agencies were deployed to ensure security during the transportation.
The flight carrying uranium for Rooppur plant was scheduled to arrive on September 24 but was not given permission to use Pakistani airspace.
According to project officials, a total of nine uranium consignments are scheduled to be brought to Bangladesh — seven for the second unit and two for the refuelling of the first unit.
All the consignments are scheduled to be delivered by December.
Fuel for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant was brought to Bangladesh in 2023.
The Rooppur plant, comprising two 1,200-megawatt units, has a total generation capacity of 2,400MW.
Construction of the plant began in 2013 with Russian assistance at an estimated cost of more than Tk1.13 lakh crore.
Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd (NPCBL) Managing Director Dr Zahidul Hasan said testing of the 16-megawatt high-pressure system under the reactor protection and safety-related system was successfully completed on Wednesday following the replacement of a defective valve.

North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul’s apology demand
item.description:
North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul’s military said Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North.
Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue.
Early Saturday, “our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea,” Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan.
“South Korea, the US, and Japan are maintaining a robust defense posture through close information sharing regarding North Korean ballistic missiles,” it said, adding the missile flew more than 700 kilometers (435 miles).
Seoul and the US-led United Nations Command found that last month’s explosion inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice, was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South side of the border.
North Korea’s military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off following leader Kim Jong Un’s designation of South Korea as his country’s “principal enemy” in 2024.
The mines responsible for the blast, which left three soldiers wounded, were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defense minister Kang Shin-chul.
South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier.
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, responded by calling Seoul “really despicable” on Friday and once again denied Pyongyang was behind the blasts.
She ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch” and said the military’s demand her country apologize was “quite ridiculous.”
Kim also warned Pyongyang was “ready for anything” Seoul might do over the mine blast -- remarks followed the next morning by North Korea’s ballistic missile launch.
Analysts said the launch would be viewed as a show of force in response to the South Korean government’s diplomatic efforts, effectively rejecting engagement.
“Seoul called for easing tensions, but Pyongyang answered by escalating them,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP.
“The message is that the North is pursuing... confrontation in response to goodwill,” he added.
South Korea’s defense minister said on Tuesday the military had “a range of necessary measures at our disposal, and we will implement them in stages” to respond to the DMZ incident, without providing further detail.
The South’s Unification Minister, Chung Dong-young, also proposed talks to address issues along the border to Pyongyang on Friday.
Kim Yo Jong, however, dismissed Chung’s suggestion of talks as a “wild dream and unilateral jargon.”
The flare-up comes at a sensitive time when US President Donald Trump’s recent overtures to Pyongyang have raised concerns that Seoul -- an ally of Washington -- could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North.
South Korea’s opposition People Power Party on Friday accused Lee of failing to criticize Pyongyang when warranted even as he takes a hard line on Ukraine for publicly disclosing the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war, an arrangement Seoul believed should be confidential.
“South Korean soldiers have been injured, and far from receiving an apology, we have been mocked by North Korea,” the opposition party said in a statement.
“We fail to see how selectively turning a blind eye to North Korea serves South Korea’s dignity or the safety of its people.”

Dhaka ranks third among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka, the densely populated capital of Bangladesh, ranked third among the world’s most polluted cities on Saturday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 170 at 9:14am.
The city’s air was classified as "unhealthy", indicating a health threat, according to the AQI report.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Kolkata and Delhi occupied the first, second, and fourth spots on the list, with AQI scores of 214, 190, and 168 respectively.
According to the AQI scale, a reading between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate", with generally acceptable air quality, though sensitive individuals should limit prolonged outdoor exertion. AQI levels of 101–150 are "unhealthy for sensitive groups", 151–200 are " unhealthy", 201–300 are "very unhealthy", and readings above 301 are considered "hazardous", posing severe health risks.
The AQI, which reports daily air quality, informs residents how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health effects. In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five key pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution. Air quality usually deteriorates in winter and improves during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that air pollution causes about seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.
